name: PPL
headline: A holding company for four regulated electric and gas utilities in Kentucky, Pennsylvania and Rhode Island.
what_short: Regulated electric and gas utilities, three states
what_it_does: PPL owns four regulated utilities. In Kentucky, LG&E and KU generate and deliver electricity and gas to 1.4 million customers. In Pennsylvania, PPL Electric delivers power to 1.5 million customers. A Rhode Island utility delivers electricity and gas. Regulators set the prices.
why_it_passed: The law grants each utility its service area and the regulators keep it, so customers have no other supplier.
Earnings come from three states and four separate regulated companies, rather than a single utility.
Insiders write down their forecast: a three-year capital plan of $17.35 billion for 2026 to 2028 with fully projected test years in Pennsylvania and Kentucky.
A Kentucky tariff for large customers brings minimum payments and collateral from data-centre customers.
why_not_now: A regulator caps what a utility may earn, so the price is far above what that capped return justifies. At $35.13 a share a buyer would earn about 2.8% to 4.2% a year, less than the 5.33% on a 30-year US Treasury bond, and the analysis's value range is only $18.20 to $18.40, about half the price.
watch: Long-term debt is $20.3 billion, and earnings cover interest only about 2.4 to 2.8 times.
The capital plan of $17.35 billion over 2026 to 2028 is large against operating cash of $2.6 billion in 2025, funded by debt, hybrid securities and new shares.
Return on equity was only about 5.1% over the period, below what regulators allow.
